FIBA Under-19 World Championship|2015 Greece]]|[[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Chinanu Michael Onuaku''' (born November 1, 1996) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Kuwait SC (basketball)|Kuwait SC]] of the [[Kuwaiti Division I Basketball League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville Cardinals]]. In 2021–22, he led the Israeli League in rebounds per game. Onuaku is known for his use of underhand [[free throw]]s, an unorthodox shooting technique most famously used by [[Rick Barry]], one of the most accurate free throw shooters in NBA history. Underhand free throws are very rarely used in the modern NBA as many NBA players view the technique as embarrassing to use; the technique is often pejoratively referred to as "granny style". Onuaku found success by adopting this shooting method, increasing his free throw percentage from 46.7% his freshman year of college to 72.4% his rookie year.{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Reichert|url=https://2ways10days.com/chinanu-onuaku-is-revitalizing-the-underhand-free-throw-300d0a4ede22|title=Chinanu Onuaku is revitalizing the underhand free throw|date=June 27, 2017|accessdate=July 13, 2023}} ==High school career== Onuaku attended [[Riverdale Baptist School]] where he averaged 12.4 points, 12.7 rebounds, and 5.5 blocks as a senior, leading Riverdale to a 30–9 record and the Capital Beltway conference title.{{cite web |title=Chinanu Onuaku - 2015-16 Men's Basketball |url=https://gocards.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/chinanu-onuaku/5058 |accessdate=August 7, 2023 |work=GoCards.com}} When Onuaku graduated, he was considered the 74th-best prospect by Rivals.com,{{cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/9868|title=Chinanu Onuaku - Rivals.com|work=Rivals.com|accessdate=December 8, 2016}} 75th by ESPN{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/146947|title=Chinanu Onuaku Basketball Recruiting|work=ESPN.com|accessdate=December 8, 2016}} and was rated as the seventh-best center in the nation by Scout.com.{{cite web|url=http://www.scout.com/player/171835-chinanu-onuaku|title=Chinanu Onuaku - Scout.com|work=Scout.com|accessdate=December 8, 2016}} ==College career== Onuaku played two seasons of college basketball for the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|University of Louisville]] between 2014 and 2016. In his sophomore season, he averaged 9.9 points, 8.5 rebounds and 2.0 blocks,{{cite web |last=Joshi |first=Hiren |date=July 20, 2016 |title=Rockets Sign Rookie Chinanu Onuaku |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-rookie-chinanu-onuaku |accessdate=June 11, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} earning All-ACC Defensive Team and All-ACC honorable mention honors and posting 11 double-doubles.{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Greer|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2016/05/25/louisville-basketball-rick-pitino-chinanu-onuaku-staying-nba-draft/84893166/|title=Final answer: Onuaku confirms NBA draft entry|work=Courier-Journal.com|date=July 20, 2016|accessdate=December 8, 2016}} In May 2016, Onuaku announced he would enter the [[NBA draft]]. ==Professional career== ===Houston Rockets (2016–2018)=== On June 23, 2016, Onuaku was selected by the [[Houston Rockets]] with the 37th overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]]{{cite web |last=Suarez |first=Paul |date=June 24, 2016 |title=Rockets Select Chinanu Onuaku and Zhou Qi in 2016 NBA Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-select-chinanu-onuaku-and-zhou-qi-2016-nba-draft |accessdate=June 11, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} and later joined them for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web |last=Joshi |first=Hiren |date=July 1, 2016 |title=Rockets to Compete in Samsung NBA Summer League 2016 |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/rockets-compete-samsung-nba-summer-league-2016 |accessdate=June 11, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} On July 20, 2016, he signed with the Rockets. He made his NBA debut on December 26, 2016, coming on in the fourth quarter and recording six points and three rebounds in a 131–115 win over the [[2016–17 Phoenix Suns season|Phoenix Suns]]. He hit a pair of free throws in the game with his underhanded free-throw action.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899909|title=Harden scores 32 points and Rockets cruise past Suns 131-115|work=ESPN.com|date=December 26, 2016|accessdate=December 27, 2016}} During his rookie season, Onuaku had multiple assignments with the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]], the Rockets' [[D-League]] affiliate.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2016-17 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|accessdate=November 28, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170126075350/http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|archive-date=January 26, 2017|url-status=dead}} On May 1, 2017, he was suspended two games without pay for pushing a game official. The incident occurred during an altercation in the final seconds of the Vipers' 122–96 loss to [[Raptors 905]] in game 3 of the 2017 NBA D-League Finals on April 27.{{cite web |date=May 1, 2017 |title=Rio Grande Valley's Chinanu Onuaku suspended |url=https://pr.nba.com/chinanu-onuaku-suspension-rio-grande-valley-vipers |accessdate=August 7, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} On August 2, 2018, Onuaku was traded from the Rockets to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for the rights to forward [[Maarty Leunen]].{{Cite web |last=Associated Press |first=The |date=August 3, 2018 |title=Mavericks get center Chinanu Onuaku in trade with Rockets |url=https://www.nba.com/news/mavericks-get-center-chinanu-onuaku-trade-rockets |access-date=June 11, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} He was waived four days later.{{cite
